quest.title: The Truth Is Also a Lie
quest.description: As you go off to send your well-wishes, Ayato gradually realizes that there is some plot at play behind this wedding. According to his reasoning, you are rapidly approaching the truth...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you doing? Release Shinnojou this instant!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Stop this at once.

dialogues.speaker: Kubo
dialogues.text: It's the Yashiro Commissioner...

dialogues.speaker: Kubo
dialogues.text: Hmph! Well, we take orders from our Master, no one else.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Really... Then, please excuse me!

dialogues.speaker: Kubo
dialogues.text: Blast! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Kubo
dialogues.text: We must report to Master right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Get back here!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: No need to follow them.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: We need bait to catch the fish anyway. Leave them be.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I think I saw a key fall to the ground during the fight. Let's free Shinnojou first.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But... in all the chaos, it must have been kicked to one side. Hmm, where did it end up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the...? It's a tanuki! ...Oh, don't tell Paimon that the tanuki took it!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Let's follow it and see.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Oh, thank the gods! You're here! Please, help me!

talks.objective: Investigate the situation inside the cave

dialogues.speaker: Yuzu
dialogues.text: Hmm, look at this... The daughter of the Kanjou Commission's Hiiragi Clan and the master of the Tenryou Commission's Kujou Clan are getting married.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Hehe... Sounds like an all-around perfect match, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Yuzu
dialogues.text: For sure. I'm just surprised, it seems very sudden. I hadn't heard a single word about it until now.

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Good luck to them, I say. I'm sure it must have been a hard decision.

talks.objective: Look for the key that the bake-danuki made off with

dialogues.speaker: Sayuri
dialogues.text: A wedding between the Kujou Clan and the Hiiragi Clan? I didn't see that coming!

dialogues.speaker: Mari
dialogues.text: A relative of mine works in the Kanjou Commission. I'll ask her about it.

dialogues.speaker: Mari
dialogues.text: She's never mentioned it before, so... I don't know...

talks.objective: Use the key to free Shinnojou

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Welcome. I just heard that the news of my wedding has been officially announced.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: It seems so sudden... I wasn't ready yet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, about that... It's kinda complicated...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You briefly explain the situation to Kujou Kamaji...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I see... So someone's trying to take advantage of our marriage...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: If you proceed with the wedding, the repercussions for you are likely to be minimal. But we must take Lady Hiiragi's situation into consideration.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I've previously considered this possibility. But in the end, we are getting married for true love, and I've promised to her that I'll do everything in my power to protect her.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I understand where you're coming from, but to be frank, she should not need your protection.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Or to put it another way, you have tacitly admitted that Lady Hiiragi will need your help to get through the hard times ahead, which perhaps suggests that, deep down, you realize all she stands to lose.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I don't mean to criticize you. It is natural to want to protect our loved ones. You're an intelligent and gentle person, and I'm sure you would have been able to think about this more objectively were you not so emotionally involved in the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I'm sure you admire Lady Hiiragi for being the independent, gentle, resilient, and strong-willed person she is.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: For the sake of marrying you, this wonderful woman will become someone who has to depend on you for the rest of her life.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Are you really okay with that?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I love her with all my heart and would do anything to make her happy...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: ...That's why I cannot abide to see her suffer or be manipulated by other people.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Yashiro Commissioner, you're right... It was naive and selfish of me to take things this far.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: But it's too late now, isn't it? There are notices everywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I have a plan. But... it needs a villain.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou, in order for my plan to work, you and I must both play the role of antagonists. But it is not without its risks.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Are you willing to help?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: If there's a way to salvage this, then let's hear it.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I've told the people at the Kanjou Commission that the marriage isn't going to unify the Kanjou Commission and the Tenryou Commission. On the contrary, it's a terrible idea that will marginalize the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The context for this is that they are planning to use this marriage to bring down the Hiiragi Clan, and the key to their success is coming up against no resistance to the marriage from the Tenryou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But what if we were to imagine for a moment that since the affairs of the Vision Hunt Decree, the Tenryou Commission has been planning to make a move against the weakened Kanjou Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The only reason you have been hesitant to act since taking over the Tenryou Commission is because you care about Lady Hiiragi's feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: And so, your plan is to liaise with the Yashiro Commission to marry her and bring her out of the Kanjou Commission as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Once that is achieved, as the person in charge of the Tenryou Commission, you no longer have any reason to hesitate.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: I see! This is an ingenious plan, and takes advantage of the situation perfectly...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This will make Hiiragi Chisato indispensable.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Exactly. Our purpose is to change Lady Hiiragi's position from an unnecessary burden to an indispensable asset.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: By doing so, we can even strengthen her position in the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Once our adversaries realize how the network of connections behind the scenes really looks, they'll do their utmost to stop this wedding from happening.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Then, we simply leave them to clear up the mess they've created.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Kamaji
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... So the network of connections... Ah, this is all way too complicated for Paimon! Can you just tell us what you need us to do?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: We have to make sure that the behind-the-scenes story comes to the attention of our dear friends in the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Matsuura, with whom I spoke earlier, will now be fearing the worst. No doubt he'll be on the lookout for the first sign of a crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: In that case, he will almost certainly have placed informants throughout Inazuma City. What we need to do is to use these informants as a breeding ground for our fake intel.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou, there are certain things that I need you to attend to personally.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Kamisato Ayato explains the details of his plan to Kujou Kamaji. A while later...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It's almost time. My ninja has located one of the informants. Let's go and see if he'll take the bait.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Thank you, thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: It was terrifying... They said they were gonna throw the cage into the sea with me still inside...

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Oh... Wait, you have to listen to me! Lady Chisato's wedding, they... It's all part of a scheme! Someone's trying to use the wedding for their own ends!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Calm down, Shinnojou. It's okay. We know about all that.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Our suspicions were roused to this possibility, and so far, everything is unfolding rather as we expected.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Those behind this plan are not going to give up easily. Their next move is imminent. We must devise sufficient countermeasures.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Yashiro Commissioner, you're personally going to take action?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: This situation has consequences for the whole Tri-Commission, and the stability of all of Inazuma is at stake. My hitherto-neutral stance ends now.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: The Almighty Shogun has always despised these pathetic power games. As a Commissioner, I am a servant of the Shogun, and it is therefore my duty to handle these tiresome matters on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Shinnojou
dialogues.text: Hmm... That's true...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Shinnojou, don't return to your post yet. Find somewhere safe and stay hidden.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon. Let's get out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A short while after leaving...

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't the Yashiro Commissioner.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I hear you showed up here with no explanation and attacked my men.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: You wouldn't happen to be carrying out some sort of secret mission, now, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: I heard that someone was taking the law into their own hands. As a responsible official of Inazuma, I could not in good conscience stand idly by.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Shinnojou may be your retainer, but the law does not grant you the right to abuse him.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Abuse? Nonsense! I was just teaching him a lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Out of nowhere, a low-ranking officer decides to barge in on Lady Hiiragi and start spurting out the most absurd and insulting nonsense one can imagine... A truly egregious loss of decorum!

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: I daresay, the poor Lady was terrified.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: So you're saying that you know absolutely nothing of the reasons for his actions? Because otherwise, why would you describe it as "out of nowhere"?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Two people from two different clans are getting married, that's all there is to it, and yet this young gentleman took it upon himself to fabricate a nonsensical disaster story around it. How should I know what he was thinking?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Even if she marries into the Kujou Clan, Lady Hiiragi will always be the daughter of the Hiiragi Clan and the most distinguished member of the Kanjou Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: We are, and always will be, her loyal assistants. It's our duty to see that she never has to worry about anything.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Loyalty and duty are our guiding principles. Not only did this guard show no regard for either, he went out of his way to upset our Lady. How could one do such a thing?

dialogues.speaker: Matsuura
dialogues.text: Even if we put it down to a rare moment of impulsivity, I have to say I'm surprised to see one of such noble standing as yourself rushing to his defense.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Darn it! This guy is good... Annoyingly good!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Funny, I'm suddenly reminded of an anecdote I'd like to share with you. There's not been a dull moment since I took up my post in the Yashiro Commission. Every day, I've been exposed to new and fascinating things.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: For instance, a merchant from abroad once told me about a curious kind of bird with the most extraordinarily long tongue. So long, in fact, that you can tie two knots in the portion of it that extends out of its beak.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I'm sure someone as erudite as yourself should be able to guess what people do with these unusual avians?

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Uh... keep them as pets?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Haha, you'd think, wouldn't you? But there's a catch. You see, this bird is of no use to humans whatsoever, and certainly doesn't make a suitable pet. If you catch one, the best thing you can do is actually cut its tongue off and throw it out of the window.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The reason they give is this: "The longest tongue has the most to say, but don't be deceived as it chirps away... lest the song it sings lead you astray."

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: You...! I say, Yashiro Commissioner, are you here simply to mock the Kanjou Commission?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Far from it. In my mind, the Kanjou Commission is made up of honorable individuals, upright and forthright, conscientious and loyal.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: It is unbecoming of such people to resort to lies, deception, and filibustering all as part of a plan to remove Lady Hiiragi from her position in the Kanjou Commission.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Yashiro Commissioner, please don't make accusations without any evidence.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: The evidence is standing right in front of me, is it not? I have a credible witness who can confirm you were quick to try and make him disappear as soon as he said something that you did not like.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Dear me, I can't believe the grand Matsuura Clan is now represented by someone with less of a sense of loyalty than even an ordinary servant.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: You studied hard and took a government position, only to make it to where you are now just to play these petty power games behind the scenes... I'm not sure whether it's because you're smart enough to play the system, or too foolish to know any better?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: In your years of service to the Shogun, not only have you managed to glean nothing good from the people around you, you have also let yourself be blinded by self-interest... And now you have ruined your once-bright future.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I'm not angry, Mr Matsuura... I just feel sorry for you.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: ...Hahaha! Is that right? Then tell me, if you're so bright, what exactly do you think you can do to me!?

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: This is at most a Kanjou Commission issue. We'll handle this amongst ourselves.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: You are reaching rather outside of your bounds, Yashiro Commissioner, if you seek to involve yourself in other clans' affairs... Might I be so bold, then, as to question your motives in doing so?

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: I think you are simply opposed to an alliance between the Kanjou Commission and Tenryou Commission, because the new balance of power in the Tri-Commission would be a threat to you personally.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: So you come here with an elaborate excuse to try and break up this marriage!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hm. So, that's how you view it. Well, I have to admit, you clearly are far more talented than I at monitoring the power balance within the Tri-Commission.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Let me be crystal clear. This wedding is going to happen, and nothing is going to change that.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: The notices have already been sent out. All of Inazuma City knows about it now!

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Most of the public weren't aware that Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato were courting, but you can bet it's all anybody's talking about now.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Once the notices go out, that's it! The wedding is a sure thing, even if it hasn't happened just yet!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Hm. I see. It seems like I was wrong.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Hah! So suddenly we see eye to eye?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I had expected you to at least be smarter than most. But it seems that I was gravely mistaken.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: Kamisato Ayato! You...! How dare you!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: You've made your move. Now, I suppose it's time I made mine.

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: ...What do you mean?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Do you seriously think this marriage will bring the Kanjou Commission and the Tenryou Commission together?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Isn't it at all possible that the Kanjou Commission becomes marginalized as a consequence of this union?

response.speaker: Matsuura
response.text: ...Hmm?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Goodness me. Well, I've learned a great deal from talking to you. That will be all for now. If you would excuse me, I shall take my leave.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, hey! What was all that? Paimon didn't follow at all!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: They had their scheme, but fortunately I was prepared. As I said, they ended up coming out from the shadows and revealing themselves.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Let's see how things are in Inazuma City. Then I'll take you through the details of my plan.

choices.text: (But he's also difficult to argue against...)

talks.objective: Check the current situation using the city Bulletin Board
Go and observe the Kanjou Commission informant

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: That person is one of Matsuura's informants.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: Let's follow him. Be careful not to get seen.

talks.objective: Follow Hideo and do not be discovered

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It's like the whole Tenryou Commission is here!

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Excuse me, has something happened on this road?

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I'm a businessman passing through, and it's a little disconcerting to see this place so heavily guarded.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Ah, please don't be alarmed. As I'm sure you've heard, the wedding of Sir Kujou Kamaji and Lady Hiiragi Chisato will take place any day now.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou decided to send for Lady Hiiragi ahead of time and have her live in Inazuma City during the run-up to the wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: We are here to clear the way for Lady Hiiragi.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Not just us, either. You'll see more Tenryou Commission members as you go further along. We're all here for the same duty.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: ...Isn't this a little excessive?

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou holds Lady Hiiragi in the highest regard and wants to treat her with the utmost respect from beginning to end.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I understand... Sorry to disturb your work.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Drat. It's exactly as Master feared.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: They say they're here to guard the road, but really they're poised to attack if Master doesn't allow Lady Hiiragi to leave Ritou...

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: Wait, no... If Lady Hiiragi does leave, they'll have all the more reason to strike... But we're in no state to defend against a Tenryou Commission attack!

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I must tell Master right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He ran off again...

choices.text: He looked like he'd seen a ghost.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: That should do it, the seeds have been sown. In this atmosphere, mounting suspicion will nurture fear among the Kanjou Commission.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Now, we wait patiently for it to grow and ferment. The calm before the storm is always the part that unsettles people the most.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are they really gonna own up and apologize, just like that?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: If you're curious to find out, you can visit the Hiiragi Clan in Ritou in a couple of days.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: I have some other business to attend to. So I won't be spending any more time on this situation.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: In any case, we've made our move. It's only a matter of time before they give up and surrender.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why are you so confident?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: This is not my first time.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
response.text: Well, then. Goodbye for now. I truly hope that things will work out in Hiiragi Chisato's best interests.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He left kind of abruptly... Are things really gonna turn out like he predicted?

choices.text: Let's keep an eye on things until the end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon too! Well, let's go to Ritou again in two days!

choices.text: I'm still a little worried about Hiiragi Chisato.
Now he realizes how serious this situation is.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Thanks for coming. Hope to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Maybe this whole "creativity" theme really will work out...

dialogues.speaker: Yuzu
dialogues.text: I wonder if they'll go anywhere nice for their honeymoon? Maybe somewhere outside Inazuma...

dialogues.speaker: Furuya Noboru
dialogues.text: Don't tell me that you're thinking of adventuring in another nation again!

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: Our duty here is to ensure the safety of this road.

dialogues.speaker: Okabayashi
dialogues.text: You'll see more Tenryou Commission members as you go further along. We're all here for the same duty. Please don't be alarmed.

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Hmm... What's with all these people coming in and out? And why does everyone look so serious?

dialogues.speaker: Tomoki
dialogues.text: Maybe I should head home early today...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, seems like he's noticed us...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Knew we should've been quieter...

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Ever may the Euthymia stand, long may the lightning shine. We are honored to hereby announce this most auspicious clime:

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Sir Kujou Kamaji, Proxy Clan Head of the Tenryou Commission,

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: And Lady Hiiragi Chisato, Proxy Clan Head of the Kanjou Commission,

dialogues.speaker: Shogunate Announcement
dialogues.text: Shall be getting married in the near future.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like the wedding is definitely going ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: It's still too early to make that conclusion. Our adversary wants to push this marriage past the point of no return. However, we can still beat them at their own game.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: But only if Kujou Kamaji is willing to help us.

dialogues.speaker: Hashimoto
dialogues.text: Did you see that? Sir Kujou Kamaji just came past here with a huge group of people.

dialogues.speaker: Nagase
dialogues.text: Could it be related to the wedding announcement?

dialogues.speaker: Hashimoto
dialogues.text: Maybe... but from the look on his face, it seems like something much more serious.

dialogues.speaker: Hashimoto
dialogues.text: He and his men seem pretty intense at the moment. Isn't it all a bit excessive for a wedding?

dialogues.speaker: Yamaue
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission has sent a load of people to Ritou. I guess it must have something to do with the wedding.

dialogues.speaker: Yamaue
dialogues.text: I think in all there must have been about a hundred people so far.

dialogues.speaker: Tokunaga
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound good. What could be going on?

dialogues.speaker: Tokunaga
dialogues.text: Ah, I hope it's just Sir Kujou Kamaji being overcautious.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: The news is spreading fast, but it appears Master's fears may be well-placed.

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: There's no way they sent this many people just to escort the bride...

dialogues.speaker: Hideo
dialogues.text: I have to investigate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He ran off...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayato
dialogues.text: As expected. Let's follow him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He was right there a moment ago... Seems he disappeared in the blink of an eye.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If only we'd made less noise..
